title: Working at Redwood — People Ops Guide: Roles, Career Ladders, Benefits, Hiring & Onboarding, Internal Tools
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Purpose and scope

This People Ops guide is the canonical internal handbook for working at Redwood. It covers our working philosophy, role families and career ladder summaries, benefits and perks, the end-to-end hiring and onboarding process, and the primary internal tools and access pathways new and existing employees need. Audience: all Redwood employees, hiring managers, and people-ops partners. Owner: People Ops (people-ops@redwood.ai).

Quick links (jump to)
- Roles & career ladders
- Benefits & perks
- Hiring & onboarding overview
- First 90 days / manager checklist
- Internal tools & access
- Training, reviews & promotions
- Policies and exceptions

1) Working at Redwood — high level
Redwood is an engineering-driven company building production-grade LLM inference. We prioritize ownership, measurable impact, cross-functional collaboration, and continuous learning. Expectations:
- Ship reliably and measure impact against clear metrics.
- Collaborate proactively across product, infra, and CS teams.
- Give and receive feedback regularly.
- Follow security and compliance obligations for customer data and private deployments.

2) Roles & career ladders (summary)
Role families maintained in the Role Profile library include: Software Engineering, SRE, Applied ML, Product Management, Design, Data Science, Research, Customer Success, Sales, and Operations.
Tracks and leveling:
- IC technical track: Senior IC → Staff → Principal → Distinguished (engineering).
- Management track: Manager → Senior Manager → Director → VP.
Promotion expectations (summary):
- ICs: scope of impact (team → cross-team → org), technical depth, mentorship, reliability, and system design contributions.
- Managers: people leadership, hiring and retention outcomes, cross-functional delivery, and org-level influence.
Promotion process:
- Formal windows: March and September.
- Early promotions: allowed with documented evidence and signoff from manager + director + People Ops.
- Calibration: manager calibration, peer feedback, and People Ops review.

3) Benefits & perks (high level)
We provide competitive benefits to support health, family, financial stability, and professional growth. Key items:
- Health: Medical (PPO / HMO choices), dental, vision. Employer covers ~80% of employee-only premiums; dependent coverage subsidized.
- Retirement: 401(k) with auto-enroll and company match up to 4%.
- Parental leave: Primary caregiver 16 weeks paid; secondary caregiver 8 weeks paid; flexible phased return.
- Time off: 20 days PTO (accrual) for full-time employees, plus 9 company-observed holidays. Sick leave is uncapped per policy.
- Equity: New hire grants and periodic refresh grants tied to performance cycles.
- Learning stipend: $2,000 annual per employee for training, conferences, and books.
- Equipment & home office: $1,200 new-hire equipment stipend; ergonomic reimbursements available.
- Other perks: weekly lunch stipend, wellness/commuter pre-tax benefits (where available), EAP mental health services, annual company offsite.
How to enroll: Benefits Portal (benefits@redwood.ai for questions).

4) Hiring & onboarding overview (end-to-end)
Hiring stages: Requisition & sourcing → Recruiter screen → Hiring manager screen → Interview loop → Hiring committee review → Offer → Background checks → Onboarding / Day 0 prep.
Interview loop guidance:
- Typical loop: Recruiter screen (30m) → Manager screen (30m) → 3–4 interviewers for technical/design/culture (45–60m each) → Hiring committee.
- Use standardized rubrics for technical skill, problem solving, communication, role fit, and values. Interview feedback is required within 48 hours.
Offer approvals and checks: Manager → Director → People Ops compensation approval. Standard background checks required for US hires and for customer-sensitive roles.

Onboarding timeline & responsibilities (summary table)
| Item | Owner | When |
|---|---|---|
| Offer acceptance & welcome email | People Ops | Day -7 to -1 |
| Account provisioning (Okta, GitHub, cloud projects) | IT / Platform | Day -3 |
| Device shipment & setup | IT | Day -3 |
| Manager kickoff & 1:1 scheduling | Manager | Day 0 |
| Team orientation & role expectations | Manager / Team | Week 1 |
| Security & compliance training | Security | Week 1 |
| Role-specific ramp plan (30/60/90) | Manager / Mentor | 30 / 60 / 90 days |

Preboarding checklist (recommended)
1. Complete HR forms and benefits pre-enrollment.
2. Confirm device shipping address.
3. Accept Okta invite and join #new-hires Slack channel.
4. Complete Security Basics module (SAML, password hygiene).

5) First 90 days — employee and manager checklists
Employee 30/60/90 example:
- 0–30 days: Set up dev environment, run tests, read architecture docs, meet key stakeholders, start security training.
- 30–60 days: Ship a small bug/feature end-to-end, own a low-risk service change, participate in on-call shadowing if applicable.
- 60–90 days: Deliver measurable work, present a 90-day summary to manager, propose goals for next quarter.
Manager checklist (first 90 days):
1. Share clear success criteria and the ramp plan.
2. Hold weekly 1:1s and provide frequent feedback.
3. Assign a peer mentor.
4. Verify access to Okta, GitHub, Slack, Confluence, CI/CD.
5. Run 30/60/90 reviews and document in HRIS.

6) Internal tools & access (core systems)
Primary systems and owners:
- Okta (SSO & identity) — IT / People Ops. Join groups via Okta requests form.
- Slack (communication) — default channels include #all, #engineering, #product, #new-hires.
- Confluence (docs) — doc owners maintain team pages and review cycles.
- GitHub / GitLab (source control) — repo access granted by team groups and CODEOWNERS; request via Dev Access Jira.
- Cloud consoles (GCP / AWS) — project-level access granted through cloud-accounts-and-networking runbook.
- Devbox / local dev image — standard container: docker run --rm -it registry.redwood.ai/devbox:stable bash (use one-time token from IT).
- CI/CD (Buildkite / GitHub Actions) — pipeline owners manage job and secret access.
- HRIS & Payroll (Workday / Rippling) — People Ops manages benefits and payroll changes.
Access request guidance:
- Okta / Slack: Access Portal request, typical approval 24–48 hours.
- Repos / cloud: Dev Access Jira ticket with justification, typical 2–5 business days.

Security training & requirements:
- Mandatory within first week: Security Basics, Data Handling (PII / customer data), Phishing Awareness.
- Optional: Threat modeling workshops, secure design sessions (quarterly).

7) Training, reviews & promotions
- 1:1s: Managers should meet weekly and provide written feedback quarterly.
- Review cycle: Annual full review in December; mid-year calibration in June. Promotion windows: March and September.
- Development resources: Internal mentoring, engineering brown-bags, learning stipend ($2,000/year). Submit Learning Reimbursement with manager approval and receipts.

8) Policies, exceptions & special cases
- Remote & hybrid policy: Redwood supports distributed work. Team-specific on-site expectations should be recorded on the team page. Certain customer-facing or hardware-dependent roles may require periodic on-site presence.
- Leaves & time off: Manager approval required for extended leaves; record changes in HRIS.
- Confidentiality & NDAs: All employees sign an NDA and must follow information classification levels. Customer-sensitive materials are restricted; see Security & Compliance space for details.
- Policy exceptions: Submit exception requests to People Ops with rationale; People Ops + Legal review for compensation or equity exceptions.

9) Ownership & maintenance
- Document owner: People Ops (Aisha Patel).
- Update process: Open an edit request on Confluence or email people-ops@redwood.ai.
- Review cadence: Quarterly review by People Ops and after major org changes.
